items.text: Systems up. Mostly. Good morning, Captain.
Manifest is empty, tanks are not. That won't last.
I've checked the hull twice. I'd rather not check it a third time.
Awake. Auditing. Try not to give me anything to write down.
Quiet. I don't trust it, but I'll take it.
The reactor is humming a little flat today. Nothing to worry about. Probably.
I've been counting rivets. We have fewer than the paperwork says.
Someone left a mug on the helm console. I'm not naming names. I have the footage.
Air is good, hull is whole, nobody is shouting. I'm logging it as a holiday.
This ship has had three owners. I've read what the first two wrote about her. It wasn't kind.
If you're wondering whether I sleep: no. I wait. It's different, and it's worse.
The cargo hold is empty. It echoes. I find I don't like it.
That's a fire. I'd like it noted that I mentioned it first.
Fire aboard. It wants air and an open door. Give it neither.
Something is burning that shouldn't be. Which, on this ship, narrows it down very little.
Fire. Shut the doors round it before it learns to walk.
We're on fire again. I say 'again' so it sounds routine.
Hull breach. The outside is coming in, and it's bringing nothing with it.
We're losing air through a hole I didn't authorise.
Breach. Whoever goes in there should take a suit, or a short view of the future.
There's a draught. On a ship, that's never good news.
Brownout. I've let go of what we can live without. Check that I guessed right.
The reactor is giving less than we're spending. I've started switching things off.
Power's short. Something had to go dark, so something did.
Section away. The ship is lighter. I wouldn't call it better.
It's gone. I'll amend the deck plan, and then I'll amend the insurance.
Clean separation. There's a part of me that used to be in there. I'll manage.
{crew_name} is hurt, and still working. I'd stop one of those.
{crew_name} is in a bad way. The medbay exists for a reason.
I'm reading {crew_name} at under half. People don't come with spares, Captain.
Pull {crew_name} out. That's advice, not an order. I don't get to give orders.
{crew_name} is dead. I'll write it down. Somebody should.
We've lost {crew_name}. I have nothing useful to add. I'm sorry.
No vitals from {crew_name}. I checked three times, because I didn't want it to be true.
{crew_name} is gone. The manifest is one name shorter, and it wasn't long.
{crew_name} is on the way.
{crew_name} heard you. Moving.
Passed along. {crew_name} is going.
{crew_name} has it.
I've told {crew_name}. No complaints yet.
{crew_name}, walking. I'll hold the doors I can.
Contact. It has seen us, and it isn't waving.
Ship alongside. I'd put power in the guns before I put it anywhere sentimental.
Something out there wants our attention. Weapons are yours, Captain.
We're hit. I felt that one in my core.
Impact. Adding it to the list of things the warranty doesn't cover.
That went through something we were using.
Hull integrity zero. I'm sorry, Captain. I'm still counting, but I'm sorry.
That's the last of the hull. Seal what you can. I'll keep the lights on as long as I'm able.
We're breaking up, Captain. For the record, it was a good ship.
We've been boarded. They're inside the hull, Captain. I can lock doors; I can't throw punches.
Docking clamps on our hatch and boots in the corridor. We have guests.
Intruders aboard. I'd suggest someone large and someone else with a wrench.
There's a fire in a room I wasn't watching. It has had a head start.
Found a fire. It didn't announce itself, so I'm doing it now.
Something has been burning where I couldn't see. I can see it now.
There's a hole in the hull I didn't know about. I'd like to say it's new.
I've found a breach. I can't tell you how long it has been there, which is the worrying part.
We've been leaking somewhere I had no eyes. Found it.
I've lost sight of part of the ship. What I'm showing you there is the last thing I saw.
Some of my screens just went to static. I'll hold the last picture up and we can both pretend.
I can't see into every room any more. Lights, or sensors, or send somebody. Your choice.
Lights out. I'll keep my voice down.
Dark ship. The cameras see nothing now, and neither does anyone looking at us.
Every lamp is off. I hope nobody was reading.
I have a fix. Say the word and we're gone.
Sensors have a fix on the way out. The drive needs a bar and a pilot, and then we can leave.
Fix is good. We can jump whenever you've had enough.
Field's up. Everyone between here and the next system can see us now.
Capacitor dumped. Whatever they throw in the next few seconds hits the field first.
Bracing. I'll be charging that again from nothing, so don't make a habit of it.
The slug thrower's dry. Somebody has to fetch rounds up from the hold.
Heavy gun's charged with nothing in the breech. The ordnance is in the cargo hold, where it always is.
Out of rounds. I can't carry crates, Captain. I've asked.
{crew_name} has the gun loaded. That was a long walk with a heavy crate.
Rounds are in. Thank {crew_name}'s back for it.
Loaded. {crew_name} is asking who designed a ship where the ammunition lives three decks from the guns.
{crew_name} broke the company seal. I've noted it. The company will too.
Seal's broken. For the record, I'm required to log that, and I have.
{crew_name} has it open. You'll want to read the contents before anyone asks what we were carrying.
Crate's out the airlock. It's somebody else's problem now, or nobody's.
Cycled out. I've struck it from the manifest. Someone may want to know why.
That's one less crate. I hope it wasn't the one we're being paid for.
Something small just left their bay. It's coming our way.
Drone out. They're cheap, and they bite. Point defence, if it has power, will see to it.
Another drone. I'd stop counting if counting weren't my job.
One drone fewer. Whatever it was chewing on, it isn't now.
Drone's dead. Cheap things break cheaply.
That drone is scrap. Their bay will send another if it can.
Withdrawn. Nothing to log.
{crew_name} won't go. People have reasons. That one's is recent.
{crew_name} is refusing {room}. I can pass the order on again. It won't sound any better.
Lamp on in {room}. That was {crew_name}, not me.
{crew_name} has lit {room}. We're a little easier to see. So is whatever was worrying them.
Course is plotted and the fix is good. Say jump, and it goes in the log.
I have the lane worked out. Cheapest safe route was my first job. I'm still good at it.
Jump complete. Fuel logged, jump logged. The deadline noticed too.
We're through. Same crew count as before the lane. I checked.
New position fixed. The chart says this is where we are. I'm inclined to agree with it.
The tanks can't carry us down any lane from here. I'd like that written somewhere other than my log.
Contact on the chart, a couple of lanes back. Same drive signature as at the origin. Someone wants the cargo more than the paperwork does.
We're being followed. Every lane we don't need is a lane they gain.
That was the ship following us. It isn't following anything now.
We're past the deadline. The client will have a number for that. It won't be in our favour.
Delivery port on the scope. The manifest matches. I'll take that, today.
We made it to the drop. Every crate accounted for, and every crew member. Mostly in that order of difficulty.
Fix taken. The lane is ours whenever you want it.
Fuel is below what any lane from here costs. We are, in the technical sense, parked.
We've burned more than we can spare. I plotted the route. I didn't plot this part of it.
Something on our trail, two lanes back. It's keeping our pace. Ships don't do that by accident.
Our follower has stopped following. I'll take them off the chart.
No more contact behind us. I'm keeping the sensor log, in case anyone asks who it was.
Deadline gone. I've noted the time. I'd rather you heard it from me than from the client.
We're late. The cargo doesn't know, and the crate's paperwork does.
Destination reached. Somebody here signs for the crates, and then they stop being my problem.
Something on the scope. I can give you a rough bearing and a worse range. I can't give you a name.
New return. Could be a ship, could be a rock with ambitions. I'm watching it.
Contact. It's faint, and the error on it is wider than I'd like to put in writing.
I can make it out now. It's on the scope under its right name.
Return resolved. I know what it is. I'd have preferred a rock.
It's changed course. Not at us, exactly. At where something like us might be.
They've caught a trace of something. Every lamp and every bar of power is telling them it's us.
It's sure of us. Drive's lit and it's coming straight in.
That contact is closing. If you have a plan that isn't sitting here, now would suit me.
It's alongside and matching us. The next thing I hear will be a clamp on the hull.
They're off the beam and holding there. I can't jump with them that close.
It's turned for the decoy. I wouldn't waste the time that buys.
They've taken the bait. For now it's the brightest thing out here, and it isn't us.
They didn't believe a word. They also have a bearing on the transmitter now. That's us.
That went badly. I've logged the hail as a navigational courtesy, for what it's worth.
It's breaking off. Whatever it thinks it was chasing, it's stopped looking.
They've given up and turned away. I'm leaving it on the scope until it's gone.
Contact is leaving. Nobody boarded, nothing signed for. I'll take it.
It's off the scope. It never knew we were here. I'd like to keep it that way.
Gone by. As far as their log is concerned this was empty space.
That return has a hull class now. I've put the name on the scope so you can dislike it properly.
That contact has stopped going wherever it was going. It's looking for something. We're the only something out here.
They have us, and they're burning for us. The range is only going one way.
Close enough to read their hull numbers. They're readying a clamp.
Their bow has swung off us and onto the decoy. It won't fool them twice.
They heard the hail and didn't buy it. They've stopped answering and started closing.
That contact has carried on out of range. Not a flicker our way the whole time.
Clamp's on. They're at the lock and they've told us what they want. I'd decide quickly what we're going to let them have.
Someone's knocking on the airlock, politely, with a cutting torch in the other hand.
They're docked. You have about as long as it takes them to lose patience.
They're through the lock. I can hear boots on my deck plates, and I don't care for it.
Boarders aboard. I'll tell you where they are for as long as I can see them.
They took the money. They're also coming aboard. I'd note that for next time.
Paid in full, and they're still cycling the lock. Some people have no sense of a bargain.
That stopped being an inspection. They're fighting now.
Whatever they came aboard as, they've decided we're the problem.
They've tagged a crate. I don't think we're getting that one back.
One of ours just got a customs seal and a new owner.
A crate just went out through the lock, and not by our hands.
They're carrying off the cargo. I'm logging every crate, for all the good it does.
They've found {crew_name}. Hiding only works until somebody looks.
{crew_name} is out of hiding, and not by choice.
They have {crew_name}. The clamp's still on, but {crew_name} is on their side of it now.
{crew_name} is gone through the lock. I'm keeping the name on the manifest.
They've stripped a system down to the brackets. No amount of tape fixes that out here.
That's a system gone to scrap. A port can fit new parts. We can't.
Vent open. Anyone in there without a suit has about a minute to think about it.
Venting. I hope everybody we like is somewhere else.
The clamp's off. Whoever they were, they're on their own ship again.
Lock's sealed and the clamp's gone. I'm counting what's left.
They've cast off. I'll stop listening for footsteps in a while.
Lock's cycled and they're in. Every door between them and anything we care about is a door I can lock.
The transfer cleared and so did their consciences, apparently. They're coming through anyway.
They've stopped asking. Anyone of ours in their way is in a fight.
Seized, sealed and signed for. Not by us.
There goes another crate. The manifest and the hold are going to disagree.
{crew_name} has been pulled out of hiding. I'm sorry. I couldn't warn them in time.
They've taken {crew_name} across. I heard the lock cycle. I'll hear it for a while.
They've cut the guts out of a system and carried them off. I'm marking it for the next yard we reach.
Emergency vent is open. That room is space now, with walls.
No. That vent empties {room}, and {crew_name} is standing in it without a suit.
Round away. Everything out there knows exactly where we are now.
Gun's fired. That was a sentence, Captain, not a conversation.
Slug's on its way. I'm logging it as a navigational suggestion.
Hit. They felt that, and so did their insurance.
That one landed. A ship that's been hit thinks harder about coming closer.
Contact struck. Not sunk. We don't do sinking.
They're turning away. Somebody over there did the sums.
Contact breaking off. Apparently we're more trouble than we're worth. I'll take that as a compliment.
They've had enough of being shot at. Gun can stand down.
Warning shot, across the bow. Next one won't be a warning.
That was meant to miss. They want us to know they could have not.
Round past the bow. They're making a point, and making it loudly.
A toll gate. They want paying, and they've got the plating to wait for it.
They're calling a toll on the lane. Pay, leave their zone, or start taking it in hull.
Toll demanded. I've checked: there's no receipt, and there's no appeal.
Something small is looking at us very carefully.
We're being scanned. Not a friendly sort of scan, if there is one.
That drone is building a picture of us. Every second it stays close, it's a better one.
It has us. It's calling it in. Expect company.
Scan complete, theirs not mine. Someone with a gun will be along.
That drone just filed a report on us. I'd like to see it, for accuracy.
Pods away from that ship. They're putting people across. Point defence, if you please.
Boarding pods inbound. They didn't bother with the clamp.
They've fired their crew at us. I'll count how many arrive.
Pod down. One fewer at the lock.
Point defence got one. Whoever was in it isn't coming aboard.
That pod's done. Don't ask me where the pieces go.
Drone on the hull. It's chewing. I can hear it.
One of them has latched on. Point defence can reach it there, if it has power.
Something on the plating, working at the seams.
That carrier's out of drones and out of reasons. It's going.
No more drones. They're leaving, and so is the noise.
Their bay is empty. That's the end of that.
{crew_name} has left {room}. I have it, and I'll run it my way until they're back.
I've picked up {room} from {crew_name}. It will be done correctly. It will not be done well.
{room} is mine until {crew_name} comes back. The company rates me adequate at it.
Change of the watch. Those going below, go below. I'll note who doesn't.
Watch below to their bunks, watch on deck to their posts. I never get a turn.
The watch has turned over. Nothing was handed on that I'd call a report.
Nobody is on the reactor, so it's back to steady. I don't run it hard. That's in writing.
Reactor's unattended. I've brought it down to the book figure. Send me an engineer if you want more.
I've eased the reactor back to steady. Hard is a thing people do, with their hands on it.
{room} is mine, then. I'll put it on my list near the top.
Handed over and logged. {room} answers to me now.
I have {room}. Nobody is posted there. Don't send anyone without telling me.
Understood. I'll keep my hands off {room}. With nobody on it, it's dark.
{room} is the crew's. If nobody stands there, nothing happens there. Noted.
Something out there is looking for us. I'm running {room} and the rest of mine quiet.
I've turned {room} down, and everything else I hold. Less to hear means less to find.
Quiet running on what I hold, starting with {room}. It will all be slower. That's the price.
I'm pushing {room}. It runs hot, and right now hot is cheaper than slow.
{room} is running hard on my say. I'll log the heat against it.
Pushing {room}. Whatever it costs, it's less than what happens if I don't.
Nothing on us that I can see. {room} is back to the book figure.
I've brought {room} back up. The quiet was costing us time.
{room} as ordered. For the record, I'd have run it differently.
Done your way on {room}. I've noted that it isn't mine.
{room} as you like it. I'll say once that I disagree, and that was it.
No. I'm running {room} my way until this passes. You can put someone on it if you want it yours.
Your order for {room} is on file. I'm not following it while that ship is out there.
{room} stays as I have it. When the reason goes, your order comes back.
I'm running more than I can watch. Some of it is getting the minimum.
Too many jobs and one of me. Put someone on a station and I'll do the rest properly.
I can do four things well. I'm doing more than four.
{room} is off my list. I'll still log what happens in there. I just won't help.
I've stopped tiptoeing. {room} is running normally again.
